still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it; the branded box still carries it beside a $29 generic on the next shelf.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and the Part D statutory exclusion for weight-loss use still stands. Medicare reaches users only through diagnosis codes that are not weight loss.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels. The FDA has approved no generic tirzepatide, so Zepbound and Mounjaro remain branded-only.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Flow arithmetic, 2032→2034 in points of adults: 19.6 current − 2.6 who stopped + 4.6 restarts from the 9.2 who were off + 8.5 new users still on = 30.1. New ever-users = 10.7 (8.5 on, 2.2 already stopped), so ever-used = 28.8 + 10.7 = 39.5. Off now = 39.5 − 30.1 = 9.4 (= 9.2 − 4.6 + 2.6 + 2.2). Cycled = 13.0 prior + 3.4 first-time restarters (of the 4.6 restarts, 1.2 were already cyclers) + 1.0 new users who stopped and restarted inside the window = 17.4; 17.4 / 39.5 ≈ 44%. One-year persistence rose from ~one-third to ~45% on generic and publicly covered product because a $0–4 copay or a $29 fill removes the cost reason for stopping. MariTide in tracks still runs ~60%. Age check: 0.20×17 + 0.33×31 + 0.24×41 + 0.23×29 = 3.4 + 10.2 + 9.8 + 6.7 ≈ 30.1. Income thirds average 30.3, bracketing the national figure. The bottom third rose most (14 → 27) through Medicaid and $29 generics. Users = 30.1% × ~274M adults ≈ 82.5M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~19.5M (24%), Medicaid ~10.5M (13%), so public ~30.0M (36%), the largest payer. Commercial ~16.0M (19%). Legitimate cash (generic retail, TrumpRx, direct, telehealth incl. ~3.4M calm subscribers) ~27.0M (33%). Gray ~9.5M (12%), down to ~6M in mid-2033 and then rebuilt. 19.5 + 10.5 + 16.0 + 27.0 + 9.5 = 82.5. Medicaid growth from 3.2M: +3.0M diabetes (PA loosened once generics arrived), +2.4M AUD route, +1.4M CV/CKD, +0.5M gambling and compulsion = 10.5M. About 9.4% of adults (~25.8M) used the drugs and are off now. Roughly 15% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, down from ~23%, now concentrated among the rural uninsured in non-expansion states, people who refuse it, and the Full Range movement. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s, ~3.1% of 12–17s (rising through Medicaid EPSDT coverage of generic semaglutide). Under-12 use holds near 0.22% after the growth communication. About 5.0M children live with a parent who regained after stopping, and ~47% of households now include a user.

access.public_coverage: Medicare is now the largest single payer, at ~19.5M users, all through non-weight codes: diabetes, CVD, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus CVD) and, since Jun 2033, alcohol use disorder. The Part D weight-loss exclusion is intact. Plans dropped most prior authorisation on CV and diabetes codes once generic semaglutide arrived at ~$40–45 net. FICTIONAL arithmetic: ~45% of Medicare fills are generic semaglutide at ~$45 net and ~55% are brands (tirzepatide for CV/OSA, Restiva, the dementia route) at ~$220 net, so 0.45×45 + 0.55×220 ≈ $141/month; 19.5M × $141 × 12 ≈ $33.0B a year, roughly flat against 2032's $31.6B while users rose 74%. Medicaid: ~10.5M users. Coverage of AUD and gambling-disorder indications is not excludable under existing federal Medicaid law, and EPSDT covers adolescents. State preferred-drug lists steer to generic injectable semaglutide through compendia listings. ~75% generic at ~$38 net and ~25% brand at ~$160 net after statutory rebates ≈ $68.5/month; 10.5M × $68.5 × 12 ≈ $8.6B a year. No state changed its weight-loss coverage policy. Seven states still cover weight use, and Kentucky and New Mexico did not return. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month, and Sun, Dr. Reddy's and Biocon now also ship FDA-approved semaglutide into the US. Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues sell for $20–60 where patents are unenforced. Canadian generics run CAD 40–70. India and China supply ~70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injection (Feb 2033, after patent settlements; Novo authorised generic) costs $29–69 cash, $29 at Cost Plus-type pharmacies and $39–49 at big chains, with copays of $0–10 on most commercial generic-first tiers. Employer coverage rebounded 30% → 38% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2034), almost all of it generic-first step therapy that requires failure on semaglutide before tirzepatide, retatrutide or amycretin. Monitored metabolic tracks hold ~7.0M enrollees within the ~16.0M commercial users. MariTide has ~6.8M users: ~5.2M in tracks and ~1.6M cash at $249, with a monthly home autoinjector launched Sep 2033. Brands hold: the Wegovy pill is $199 maintenance and $149 to start at TrumpRx, Zepbound $249–299, retatrutide ~$399 cash, amycretin on prior-authorisation formularies. No oral generic exists because the SNAC formulation patents run to the 2030s. Gray market ~9.5M: compounded or 'research' retatrutide ~3.5M at $60–90; tirzepatide analogues and counterfeit pens ~2.5M; 'monthly' semaglutide or retatrutide depot vials ~1.5M, none approved; compounded amylin blends ~1.0M; residual Indian semaglutide ~1.0M. Generic semaglutide gutted counterfeit semaglutide; demand moved up to the high-efficacy molecules that remain branded.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; US generics since Feb 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide; clinic and, since Sep 2033, home autoinjector)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; Restiva, for AUD and gambling disorder)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody adjunct for lean-mass preservation (bimagrumab, approved Oct 2033; not an incretin)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide incl. generics, liraglutide, Wegovy pill)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; growth-monitoring label)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide)
alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, as Restiva, Jun 2033)
gambling disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, as Restiva, Mar 2034): the first behavioural-compulsion indication
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' plans (low-dose oral semaglutide, Foundayo, or now microdosed generic semaglutide injection), ~3.4M subscribers
compulsive shopping, sports-betting 'cool-off' and screen-compulsion use, prescribed by telehealth on the strength of the gambling label
dementia prevention in 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash or gray
AUD coding of mild or social drinkers to reach Medicaid or Part D coverage for what is in practice weight use
microdosing for 'steadiness' recommended by employer wellness coaches
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Generic semaglutide injection was approved Feb 2033 after patent settlements, with a Novo authorised generic. This is the generic_collapse mechanism. Oral semaglutide and tirzepatide have no generics. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) was approved Jun 2033 and sold as Restiva. The compulsive_behaviour driver is realised through Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3, which read out positive Sep 2032 and was filed Nov 2032. Approval came Mar 2034, 16 months after filing. Compulsive-buying and problematic-gaming trials are in phase 2 and are not labelled. Bimagrumab, filed Jul 2032, was approved Oct 2033 as an adjunct for adults 65+ at ~$900/month list and is rarely covered. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in Jun 2034 with a modest benefit and a persistent fracture excess, and Lilly resubmitted in Oct 2034 with a decision due in 2035. The monthly driver is realised through MariTide's scale (~6.8M users) and its home autoinjector. Implant programmes are in phase 2 and not on the market. Unapproved 'monthly depot' vials circulate in the gray market. The global incretin market is ~$158B (2034), down from its peak as US semaglutide revenue fell ~45%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of stopping outside clinic tracks. New generic starters with less titration support report more early vomiting. Chronic diarrhoea is routinely worked up for EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; generics carry identical labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute cases rise with the user base.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis. Litigation centres on EPI, and generic makers are now co-defendants.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR stays ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. With 65+ use at 29%, absolute fractures attributable to incretins rise. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial confirmed the excess.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab approved as an adjunct for 65+ (Oct 2033) but rarely covered.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The Sentinel anhedonia study found no suicidality signal in adults, including AUD and gambling-disorder populations.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing study (Sentinel claims, n≈210,000, with an 18,000-person SHAPS patient-reported sub-cohort; published Oct 2033) estimated clinically meaningful anhedonia at 6.9% of users at maintenance doses vs 3.0% of matched controls, 10.4% on retatrutide and 7.8% on tirzepatide. At calm-plan doses it was 4.0% vs 3.0%, with a confidence interval crossing null. Onset is mostly within 6 months, and symptoms resolved within 3 months of stopping in ~80%. With ~82M users, that is roughly 2.5–3M excess cases nationally.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions 'Anhedonia and emotional blunting' (Nov 2033), with prevalence figures in the label and Medication Guide and advice to ask about pleasure and motivation at follow-up. No REMS. The same mechanism underlies the AUD and gambling indications. Telehealth calm advertising falls under FTC rather than FDA jurisdiction, and no enforcement followed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Gray retatrutide users who lose a supplier regain fastest.
B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. The low-ferritin signal in adolescent girls persists as Medicaid adolescent use grows.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on labels; Medicaid labs often not completed.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years on semaglutide is confirmed, with partial recovery in about half after stopping for 12+ months. Tirzepatide 7-year data show a smaller excess (HR ~1.3) that is now nominally significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class EPI warning carried onto all generic labels; tirzepatide label update under negotiation.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The cycling cohort (~17.4% of adults have cycled) is now large enough to study, and bone and pancreatic findings are pending.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs continue; NIH cycling cohort funded under existing appropriations.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Counterfeit semaglutide reports fell sharply after generics arrived, then harms shifted to compounded retatrutide and 'monthly' depots. In May 2034 the CDC reported ~410 cases of severe prolonged vomiting and tachycardia from depot vials that released most of their dose in the first week, plus ~150 injection-site abscesses. Seven deaths are attributed in 2033–34. Total non-approved-product adverse-event reports have passed ~31,000.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to 503A compounders and 'research peptide' sites; import alert extended to retatrutide API makers; no statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 36-month liraglutide PMR update shows a height-velocity deficit of ~0.6 cm/year in children who were prepubertal at start, with partial catch-up in some who stopped. The Swedish ARFID HR holds at ~1.8. Adolescent starts are growing fastest under Medicaid, where 6-monthly growth checks are documented in ~55% of charts against ~85% commercially.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Feb 2032 Drug Safety Communication and growth-monitoring label stand; EMA added similar wording (2033); no age restriction.

safety_ledger.effect: Discontinuation rebound in AUD and gambling-disorder patients (craving and mood dip after stopping)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Early Restiva registry data suggest relapse to heavy drinking or wagering in ~40% within 6 months of stopping, similar to other AUD pharmacotherapy. Some patients report a transient low mood in weeks 2–6 off drug. The data are uncontrolled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None yet; part of postmarketing commitments on the Restiva approvals.

food_and_beverage.state: About 47% of US households include a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14–16% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~12–13%. The 2032 strategy of value packs for lower-income zip codes stopped working once Medicaid and $29 generics reached those zip codes, and Dollar General and Family Dollar report snack unit declines in 2034. PepsiCo consolidated two Frito-Lay plants, in Kentucky and Arizona. Protein bays have spread to mass grocery.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~19% from 2025 and beer ~12%. Restiva's AUD indication puts the drug in front of the heaviest drinkers through Medicaid and Part D, and calm plans bundle 'drink less'. Diageo and Pernod cut US distribution headcount. Midwestern bar closures continue, and Full Range supper clubs are small new buyers of craft spirits.

restaurants.state: Traffic is down ~2% over two years. QSR value-menu growth in lower-income markets stalled as public coverage spread. Portion tiers are universal in casual dining. A small 'long table' segment of Full Range supper clubs and fixed-menu dinners is growing in Nashville, Asheville and Portland, Maine.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue to shrink. Lane Bryant runs as a shop-in-shop. Resale, stretch and rental serve cyclers. A Full Range womenswear niche (soft tailoring, cut for bodies that are not changing) gets press out of proportion to its sales.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans add resistance-training benefits, citing fracture data. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–400. Budget chains' $39 lean-mass add-on is their best-selling upsell.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend fell to ~+2% on generic-first step therapy, and employer coverage rebounded to 38%. Adherence differentials persist in self-insured firms. Part D premiums were flat for 2034 for the first time in five years. Medicaid incretin spend is ~$8.6B a year, and states complain about AUD 'code drift' but have not changed policy.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell ~45% after generics, and it leans on Restiva and orals. Lilly holds the high-efficacy tier with tirzepatide and retatrutide, and Amgen's MariTide grows on track volume. Viatris, Sun, Dr. Reddy's, Teva and Biocon split US generic semaglutide. Counterfeit-defence spending shifted to retatrutide.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thin used to signal money and now signals almost nothing, because a $29 generic and a Medicaid copay put it within reach of most people. What still reads is texture and choice. Lifted, scanned muscle means coached. Thin and soft means generic or public. A monthly bruise means an employer track. A face that swings by 30 pounds each year means a gray-market cycler. The newest signal is an unmedicated body that is visibly unbothered, worn on purpose.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class markers inverted at the top. In Nashville and Asheville the Full Range network, mostly college-educated women aged 25–45 plus a wing of evangelical families, treats being unmedicated as a discipline and a luxury: a body allowed to want things. In Charlotte and Austin 'off-drug lean' remains the elite boast. In Memphis and the Delta the bottom third now looks like everyone else on generic semaglutide, and the cycler's face belongs mostly to retatrutide buyers in the middle third chasing bigger losses. Upper-income parents keep children off. Medicaid adolescents are the fastest-growing young users.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter almost everywhere except Full Range tables, where the four-hour dinner is the point. Bread Alone claims ~700 congregations. Protein remains a hospitality marker. Thanksgiving coverage in 2033 ran 'the half-medicated table' as a lifestyle trope.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'Full Range' and 'unmedicated' filters, and the anhedonia label gave couples a shared vocabulary. 'Range mismatch' is the new presenting complaint, and some couples' therapists now ask SHAPS questions at intake. 'Lean-mass verified' badges persist but feel dated.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Among the medicated majority appetite is a symptom that is managed. For Full Range it is evidence of being alive, and 'I want things' is printed on tote bags. Unmuted folded much of its membership into Full Range. Fat-acceptance revivalists remain separate and accuse Full Range of making thin women's appetite into a status display. MAHA-aligned groups court Full Range on children and the 'drugged nation' line.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The labelled rate is 6.9% vs 3.0% at maintenance doses, 10.4% on retatrutide, and 4.0% vs 3.0% (not significant) at calm-plan doses. Across ~82M users that implies ~2.5–3M excess clinically meaningful cases. ~3.4M people pay for calm and focus plans at $29–199 for the drug plus a $39–59 platform fee. Platforms now quote the label's low-dose figure as 'FDA-studied evenness'.
interior_life.framing: The same pharmacology appears three ways on a label: a Warnings and Precautions entry (anhedonia), two indications (AUD, gambling disorder) and, off-label, a subscription product (calm). Telehealth calls it evenness. Clinicians call it a labelled adverse effect. Full Range calls it the flattening. Sportsbooks call it churn.
interior_life.effect_on_work: ~7.0M employees are in adherence-verified tracks. Wellness vendors added 'motivation check-ins' after the label, which gives them a new data stream. Some EAPs offer Restiva for gambling and shopping. One EEOC ADA charge was closed without cause finding in 2033 and the other remains pending. Upper-tier firms still don't monitor, and 'focus protocol' remains a résumé-adjacent boast.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account is down ~8% since 2032 in medicated suburbs. DraftKings cites incretins in a 10-K risk factor, and the gambling-disorder label made it a disclosed risk. New Jersey and Ohio betting tax receipts dipped modestly. Full Range has a scene of loud supper clubs, maximalist food photography and a Nashville songwriting circle whose 'range songs' chart on streaming. Calm-plan subscribers remain the target audience for ambient series.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The anhedonia label made 'are you flat or am I' an answerable question. Couples now cite the 6.9% figure. Some partners time drug holidays around anniversaries. Desire mismatch remains the top couples complaint, and Full Range dating events advertise 'all feelings welcome'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No state acted on adherence premiums, calm marketing or children. Full Range and MAHA-aligned legislators held joint hearings in Tennessee and Texas on 'drugging kids on Medicaid' and passed nothing. Gaming industry lobbyists quietly opposed Medicaid coverage of Restiva for gambling and failed, because federal law gave states no option. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence, though campaign consultants now segment 'calm-plan households' for message testing.

state.regulatory_posture: Routine and permissive. The FDA approved generic semaglutide, two Restiva indications and bimagrumab, and labelled anhedonia with a prevalence estimate. It sent warning letters to compounders without new enforcement authority. CMS applied existing law to new labels. No state legislature acted and Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. Public coverage widened because new non-weight indications triggered existing Medicaid and Part D obligations and because generic prices let plans drop prior authorisation. TrumpRx continues on manufacturer-set prices, and the 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, wider in practice. MariTide home-pen apps log injections to wellness vendors under consent. Post-label 'motivation check-ins' add mood data. Calm platforms sell de-identified focus and motivation cohorts to benefits brokers and now to political data firms. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers Restiva for AUD under existing rules. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT still has not ruled on Restiva, calm-plan or off-label use in commercial drivers, and some carriers added anhedonia questions to fitness-for-duty forms on their own.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian firms now supply most US generic semaglutide legally, which eased the CBP enforcement fight over semaglutide. The gray-market fight moved to Chinese retatrutide and depot API. The FDA named three more Chinese makers in 2034, and Beijing protested again.

events.event: FDA approves first generic semaglutide injections from Viatris, Sun Pharma and Dr. Reddy's after patent settlements with Novo Nordisk, which launches its own authorised generic; by mid-2034 a month's supply costs $29–69 in cash

FDA approves oral semaglutide, branded Restiva, for alcohol use disorder; CMS tells states the indication falls under mandatory Medicaid drug coverage and outside the Part D weight-loss exclusion, and Medicare and Medicaid incretin users pass 30 million by late 2034

FDA adds an 'anhedonia and emotional blunting' warning to all incretin labels after its Sentinel study finds 6.9% of users affected against 3.0% of controls, 10.4% on retatrutide; telehealth calm plans cite the study's non-significant low-dose figure in new ads

Restiva becomes the first drug approved for gambling disorder, 16 months after Novo filed on a positive phase 3; telehealth firms begin prescribing it off-label for compulsive shopping and sports-betting 'cool-offs'

CDC links unapproved 'monthly' semaglutide and retatrutide depot vials sold by compounders and Telegram shops to ~410 severe overdose-pattern cases and ~150 abscesses; gray-market use, down to ~6M after generics, is back near 9.5M on demand for retatrutide copies, while Amgen's legal monthly MariTide home pen passes 6.8M users

The Nashville-founded Full Range network, which pledges members to stay unmedicated, reports 1.1 million pledges and 300 supper-club chapters, and holds a joint Tennessee legislative hearing with MAHA-aligned lawmakers on Medicaid adolescent prescribing; no bill advances

open_tensions: The label names reward blunting as a harm in one section and sells it as treatment in another. Restiva's gambling and AUD indications and the 3.4M calm subscribers rest on the same mechanism as the 2.5–3M excess anhedonia cases, and no agency owns the calm advertising.

Public programmes became the default payer without any law changing, through non-weight codes. 'AUD code drift' in Medicaid and the dementia route in Medicare are how weight use gets paid for, and every state budget office knows it. Meanwhile gambling and alcohol tax receipts fall slightly.

Generic semaglutide emptied the counterfeit semaglutide market but not the gray market. ~9.5M people buy retatrutide copies and unapproved monthly depots because the 24% molecules stay branded at $399, and the 2034 depot cluster shows the harms have moved up the efficacy ladder.

Adolescent incretin use is now growing fastest under Medicaid, where growth checks are documented in barely half of charts. Upper-income families keep children off, and nobody yet knows final adult height.

prose.headline: Thirty Percent and a $29 Pen: America Got Its Drug Cheap, Put It on Medicaid, and Named the Flatness on the Label
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 about three American adults in ten take an incretin drug, roughly eighty-two million people, and four in ten have tried one. The number jumped by more than ten points in two years. The reason was price, not persuasion. In February 2033 generic semaglutide injections reached American pharmacies after Novo Nordisk settled its patent fights, and within a year a month's supply cost $29 at the cheapest counters and under $50 almost everywhere else. The branded box beside it still says $1,349.

The cheap pen did more than lower the price. It changed who pays. Medicare still cannot pay for weight loss, and Congress never changed that. It can pay for diabetes, heart disease, kidney disease and, since June 2033, alcohol use disorder, when the FDA approved an oral semaglutide called Restiva. Medicaid has to cover approved treatments for addiction. Once generics made the drug cheap, plans stopped fighting prior authorisations, and clinicians found a diagnosis code for almost anyone who needed one. Thirty million people now get the drug through public programmes, more than through employers. Medicare's bill barely moved. The government became the main payer without anyone voting for it.

In March 2034 Restiva became the first drug approved for gambling disorder. Sportsbooks noticed before anyone else did. Telehealth companies noticed next and began prescribing it for shopping, scrolling and the Sunday-afternoon betting app.

In November 2033 the FDA put a warning on the label about the thing these drugs had always been rumoured to do. Its large study found that about seven in a hundred users lose a real share of their capacity for pleasure, against three in a hundred who are not on the drug, and about one in ten on retatrutide. At the low doses sold as 'calm' plans the difference was too small to call. The calm companies put that sentence in their advertising. More than three million people now subscribe. The same effect is a warning in one section of the label, a treatment in another, and a product sold off-label.

The gray market shrank and came back. Counterfeit semaglutide stopped making sense at $29, and buyers moved to the molecules that are still branded and still lose the most weight. About nine and a half million people buy copied retatrutide from compounders and Telegram shops, or 'monthly' depot vials that no regulator has approved. In May 2034 some of those vials released a month's dose in a week, and hundreds of people ended up in emergency rooms. Amgen's legal monthly pen, MariTide, has nearly seven million users. Many of them inject at home on a day their wellness app records.

When something is cheap and nearly universal it stops signalling status, and the signal moves somewhere else. In Nashville a network called Full Range asks members to pledge to stay unmedicated. It counts more than a million pledges, and its supper clubs serve four-hour dinners to women who want it known that they still want things. It holds hearings with MAHA-aligned legislators about teenagers on Medicaid starting semaglutide, because that is where adolescent use is growing and where growth charts are least often filled in. No bill has passed. No state acted on anything.

In Memphis the bottom third looks like everyone else now. The visible cycler is the middle-income retatrutide buyer whose supplier went quiet. Snack plants consolidate, bars close and Part D premiums held flat this year. Couples quote the 6.9 percent figure to each other. The country looks calmer than it did, and some of that calm is a side effect printed on the label.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tanya Ruiz pulls the pen from the butter compartment at 6:10, before the kids are up. Generic semaglutide. TennCare, three-dollar copay. The clinic wrote 'alcohol use disorder, mild' after she admitted to four nights of boxed wine a week, and the nurse practitioner did not look up when she typed it.

She drives to her first client in Whitehaven, Mr. Odom, eighty-one, who is on Zepbound through Medicare for his heart and complains it makes the cornbread taste like paper. She cuts it small for him anyway.

At lunch she reads the folded leaflet that came with her refill. Section 5.9. Anhedonia and emotional blunting. 6.9 percent. She tries to remember the last thing she was excited about and lands on her daughter's choir solo in October, which counts.

Her husband Luis texts a photo of a vial with a Telegram handle on the label. Reta. Eighty dollars. His supplier's back. She types don't, deletes it, and sends a thumbs up.

After school, Marisol, fifteen, wants to know if she can start the shots too. Half of tenth grade is on them. The school nurse handed out a sheet about growth checks every six months. Tanya says they'll ask Dr. Patel and knows the appointment is in March.

Her sister Dee calls from Nashville, from a Full Range dinner, loud and laughing behind the phone, a table of women eating peach cobbler on purpose. Dee says, you sound tired. Tanya says she's fine.

At nine she sits on the porch with a cup of tea. She does not want the wine. She does not want much of anything. It is a quiet night, and she can't tell whether she likes it.
